title: Hourly to Annual Pay: National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates and Kia Salary Sacrifice
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual salary with our guide. Compare National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, and kia salary sacrifice for 38-hour weeks.
salarySummary: Based on a 38-hour week, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, equating to $52,249.44 annually before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week (typically 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $30 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $59,280 per year. This assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime or penalty rates.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and an award rate?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum pay for all employees not covered by an award or agreement, currently $26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026. Award rates are set by the Fair Work Commission for specific industries and occupations, and are often higher. Always check your award via the Fair Work Ombudsman.

faqs.q: How does kia salary sacrifice affect my take-home pay and super?
faqs.a: A kia salary sacrifice arrangement reduces your taxable income by diverting part of your pre-tax salary towards a car lease. This can lower your tax bill, but the super guarantee (12% of ordinary earnings) is still calculated on your original ordinary earnings, not the sacrificed amount. The calculator on this site does not deduct salary sacrifice.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Hourly to Annual Conversion

When you’re comparing a job offer or negotiating a pay rise, it helps to see your hourly rate as an annual figure. The standard formula is simple: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, that’s **hourly rate × 38 × 52**. This gives you your gross annual salary before tax, super, and any deductions.

For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. Using the formula: $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,249.44 per year. If you’re a casual employee, the minimum casual rate is $33.05 per hour (including 25% casual loading), which works out to $65,311.60 annually.

### Why 38 Hours and the Fortnight?

Australia’s standard full-time week is 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Act. Many awards and agreements use this as the base. When you’re paid fortnightly, your gross pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. For the National Minimum Wage, that’s $1,004.90 per week or $2,009.80 per fortnight. Knowing your fortnightly amount can help with budgeting and comparing salary packages.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor – no adult employee can be paid less than $26.44 per hour (or $33.05 casual). However, most industries have award rates that are higher. For instance, the Hospitality Industry General Award may set different rates for different roles. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides for each award. These rates are averages for the industry or state, not a median for your specific job. Always check your classification in the relevant award.

Award rates often include penalty rates for weekends, public holidays, or late nights. The simple annual conversion here assumes no penalty rates, no allowances, and no unpaid overtime. It’s a baseline estimate.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. This loading is part of your ordinary earnings, so superannuation is calculated on the loaded rate. For example, a casual on the minimum wage earns $33.05 per hour, and super at 12% adds $3.97 per hour on top – paid into your super fund, not to you directly.

The super guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. If your annual ordinary earnings exceed that cap, super is only paid on the first $270,830. The calculator on this site estimates super at 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Once you have your gross annual figure, tax is deducted using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15c for each $1 over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30c for each $1 over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37c for each $1 over $135,000
- $190,001 and above: $51,370 plus 45c for each $1 over $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (using the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds). The calculator does not deduct HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

### Kia Salary Sacrifice

If you’re considering a **kia salary sacrifice** arrangement, it can reduce your taxable income by having part of your pre-tax salary used to pay for a car lease. This lowers the amount of tax you pay, but it does not change the super guarantee calculation – super is still based on your ordinary earnings before the sacrifice. The calculator on this site does not account for salary sacrifice, so your actual take-home pay may differ. Always consult a tax professional.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

To convert your own hourly rate, visit [the timesheet](/) and type your base hourly rate. If you’re a casual, tick the checkbox to add 25% casual loading – do not type a rate that already includes loading. The calculator will show your annual gross, fortnightly pay, estimated tax, and super. For award rates, refer to [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman. You can also check [reference tables](/data) for more benchmarks.

### Summary

- Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 (assume 38 hours for full-time).
- Fortnightly pay = weekly pay × 2.
- National Minimum Wage: $26.44/hr ($33.05 casual).
- Award rates vary; check your award.
- Super is 12% on top of ordinary earnings, up to $270,830.
- Tax uses 2026–27 resident rates plus 2% Medicare.
- Salary sacrifice (like kia salary sacrifice) affects tax but not super calculations.

This is an estimate only. For a binding determination of your pay, consult the Fair Work Ombudsman or a qualified advisor.
